title: NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Models Launch for World Simulation
summary: NVIDIA releases Cosmos 3 open models for interactive world simulation. New physical world models enable robotics, autonomous systems, and simulation tasks.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- NVIDIA released Cosmos 3, a new family of open-source models designed specifically for interactive physical world simulation and robotics applications.
- The models enable developers to generate and manipulate realistic simulations for autonomous vehicles, robotics training, and synthetic data generation workflows.
- Cosmos 3 is now available on Hugging Face, providing researchers and enterprises with accessible tools for building world models without proprietary constraints.


NVIDIA has released Cosmos 3, a new generation of open-source physical world foundation models designed for interactive simulation environments. Officially launched on November 5, 2026, the models enable developers to generate, manipulate, and interact with realistic simulations for robotics, autonomous systems, and synthetic data generation. The release marks a significant expansion in accessible world modeling capabilities for research and enterprise applications.


## What Cosmos 3 Models Deliver


Cosmos 3 provides a suite of models trained on massive datasets of physical world interactions, vehicle dynamics, and robotic manipulation scenarios. The models can generate video sequences that respond to interactive inputs, allowing developers to simulate how objects, agents, and environments behave under different conditions. This capability is critical for training autonomous vehicles, testing robotic control systems, and creating synthetic datasets that reflect real-world physics.


The models support conditional generation, meaning users can specify initial states, actions, or environmental parameters and receive coherent simulation outputs. This approach reduces the need for expensive real-world data collection and enables faster iteration cycles in development pipelines.


## Release Date and Availability


The Cosmos 3 models were officially released on November 5, 2026, and are now available on Hugging Face. NVIDIA has made the models freely accessible under an open-source license, allowing researchers, startups, and enterprises to integrate them into their workflows without licensing fees. The release includes model weights, inference code, and documentation for deployment on NVIDIA GPUs.


## Technical Architecture and Capabilities


Cosmos 3 builds on advances in video generation and world modeling, leveraging transformer-based architectures optimized for temporal consistency and physical plausibility. The models are trained to understand causal relationships between actions and outcomes, enabling them to predict future states based on current inputs. Key capabilities include:


- Multi-view scene generation with consistent geometry across viewpoints
- Responsive simulation that incorporates user-defined control signals
- Long-horizon prediction for extended simulation sequences
- Integration with robotics frameworks for real-time control applications


The models are designed to work alongside existing simulation tools, providing a foundation layer that can be fine-tuned for domain-specific tasks such as warehouse automation, surgical robotics, or autonomous driving in complex urban environments.


## Use Cases for Developers and Researchers


Cosmos 3 targets several high-value use cases in AI and robotics development. Autonomous vehicle teams can use the models to generate diverse driving scenarios, including edge cases that are rare in real-world datasets. Robotics researchers can simulate manipulation tasks without requiring physical hardware, accelerating the training of control policies. Synthetic data pipelines can leverage the models to create labeled datasets for computer vision and perception systems.


The open-source nature of the release lowers barriers for academic labs and smaller companies that lack access to proprietary simulation platforms. By providing state-of-the-art world modeling capabilities without vendor lock-in, NVIDIA is enabling a broader ecosystem of developers to build on these foundational technologies.


## What This Means


The launch of Cosmos 3 represents a strategic move by NVIDIA to democratize access to physical world modeling technologies. By releasing the models as open-source, NVIDIA positions itself at the center of the robotics and simulation AI ecosystem while accelerating innovation across the industry. For developers, Cosmos 3 offers a powerful new tool for building and testing systems that interact with the physical world, reducing development costs and timelines. As[world models](https://emergent.sh/news/world-models-ai) become more capable, they will play an increasingly central role in how autonomous systems are trained, validated, and deployed at scale.
